title: Cash App fraud-control failures produce a formal redress obligation while individual correction and receipt remain unobserved
source_unit: CFPB enforcement action, Block consent order, and CFPB payment-by-case status for Cash App fraud and dispute handling
geography: United States Cash App users and consumers covered by the Block enforcement order

observations.period: January 16, 2025 CFPB enforcement action and consent-order remedy

denominator.unit: unauthorized-transfer claims reported in the order as lacking required timely provisional credit when investigations exceeded 10 business days

civil_penalty.unit: U.S. dollars separate from consumer redress

frozen_account_class.value: account frozen at least 14 days with a balance of at least $25; the order assigns a $50 redress component to each affected consumer in that class
frozen_account_class.unit: defined affected class and remedy component

recipient_receipt.unit: missing final affected-consumer list, payment date, per-person amount, account correction, receipt, adequacy, and residual-loss outcomes

observations.method: Extraction from the official CFPB enforcement action and Block consent order; reported claims, class definitions, ordered redress, civil penalty, and post-plan reporting requirements are kept separate from person-level recovery.
observations.uncertainty: The 153,866 claims are not a population incidence estimate or a stable person-level denominator. An ordered redress range and required future report do not establish implementation, account correction, payment, receipt, or adequate recovery.
observations.subgroup: Cash App users with fraud-related disputes, including the order-defined frozen-account class; public records do not expose demographic, financial, disability, language, or access subgroups.
observations.counterinterpretation: A formal operational correction and redress obligation can coexist with unresolved individual loss, effort, access, and trust because the order's reporting contract is not itself a completed payment record.

denominator.unit: CFPB payments-by-case public index checked for a Block/Cash App distribution entry

public_distribution_listing.value: No Block or Cash App entry located in the ongoing or closed case lists at recheck

redress_contact_route.value: The Block case page still provides a redress contact route and says consumers do not need to take action at this time to obtain redress

payment_or_receipt.value: not observed in the public index
payment_or_receipt.unit: absence of a public recipient-level distribution report; not evidence that no payment occurred

observations.method: Dated recheck of the CFPB payments-by-case index and current Block case page; absence from the public list is retained as a bounded visibility result, not a nonpayment finding.
observations.uncertainty: Company-administered payments, unpublished distributions, or later reports could exist outside the public index. No person-level payment, account correction, receipt, residual loss, continued use, switching, trust, or exit data are exposed.
observations.subgroup: Consumers covered by the Block/Cash App order; no subgroup-level distribution status is public.
observations.counterinterpretation: A missing public case-list entry may reflect route, publication timing, or company administration rather than nonpayment or remedy failure.

related_sources.claim: The CFPB describes the enforcement action, operational failures, ordered redress, and civil penalty.
The CFPB Block docket provides the official case and order context.
The current Block case page provides the redress contact route and public process status.

boundary: This record follows Cash App fraud-related dispute exposure through CFPB enforcement, operational correction, and an ordered redress obligation, then records the public distribution-status boundary. It does not estimate user harm, payment receipt, account correction, adequacy, trust repair, continued use, switching, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Block consent order PDF and CFPB payments-by-case HTML page were directly retrieved and hashed on 2026-10-20; project ledger preserves the compact extraction and explicit missingness boundary.
